title: Agents: tools, the loop and when to stop
summary: A dependable agent is the reason-act-observe loop plus careful handling of everything that goes wrong. Tools are described by a name, a description and a JSON schema (best generated from the function signature). Arguments are validated before running, and errors come back as readable observations rather than crashes. Long outputs are truncated or stored behind a handle. Budgets on steps, tokens and time, plus repetition detection, stop runaway loops. Use a fixed workflow when the steps are known, an agent when they are not, and confirm irreversible actions with a person.
llm_link: Tool calling is next-token prediction in a format the model was fine-tuned on (lesson 10.6). Everything in this lesson lives in the harness, and it is what turns that ability into an agent you can leave running.
key_ideas: A tool = name + description + argument schema. The description is part of the prompt: it is how the model decides when and how to call the tool.
Validate arguments against the schema before running; return errors (validation or the tool's own) as plain-language observations so the model can correct itself.
Cap observation size: keep the start (and often the end) with a note, or store the full output and return a handle the agent can page through.
Stop on an answer, and also on budgets (steps, tokens, time) and on repetition (the same call with the same arguments twice).
Workflow (code decides the steps) when the path is known; agent (model decides) when it is not. Require human confirmation for irreversible actions.

quiz.q: A tool raises an exception because a date argument is in the wrong format. What should the agent loop do?
options: Crash so a developer notices
Return the error message to the model as an observation and let it try again
Silently skip the step
Restart the whole task
quiz.explain: Errors are information. Written back as text ('date must be YYYY-MM-DD'), they usually let the model fix the call on the next step.

quiz.q: Why truncate a tool's output before appending it to the context?
options: Models cannot read numbers
A huge output can crowd everything else out of the context window and makes every later step slower and costlier
Truncation improves accuracy of the tool
Tool outputs are not allowed in the context
quiz.explain: Every later step rereads the whole transcript. Keep a bounded excerpt with a note, or a handle to fetch more on demand.

quiz.q: Predict what a good loop does: the model requests search(query='refund') with the same arguments twice in a row.
options: Run it again; results may differ
Treat it as a sign the agent is stuck and stop (or intervene)
Ignore the second call and continue
Switch to a different model
quiz.explain: An identical repeated call usually means the agent is circling. Detecting it, alongside step and token budgets, prevents runaway loops.

quiz.q: Monthly invoices are always processed in the same four steps. What should you build?
options: An autonomous agent with many tools
A workflow: ordinary code that calls the model at fixed points
A subagent per invoice
Nothing; models cannot do this
quiz.explain: When the path is known in advance, a workflow is cheaper, faster and far easier to test. Agents earn their place when the next step depends on what was just observed.

quiz.q: In an LLM agent, how does the model 'know' a tool exists and what arguments it takes?
options: It reads the tool's source code at runtime
From the tool's name, description and schema placed in its context, in the format it was fine-tuned on
Tools are compiled into the weights
The harness guesses on its behalf
quiz.explain: The model only sees tokens. The tool definition in the prompt, written well, is what steers it to call the right tool with valid arguments.

problems.title: A tool schema from a Python function
problems.prompt:
Write tool_schema(fn), which describes a function the way a tool-calling API expects. Use inspect.signature for the parameters and their type annotations, and the first line of the docstring as the description.

def get_weather(city: str, days: int = 1):
    """Forecast for a city, for 1-7 days."""

tool_schema(get_weather) ==
{'name': 'get_weather', 'description': 'Forecast for a city, for 1-7 days.',
 'parameters': {'type': 'object',
                'properties': {'city': {'type': 'string'}, 'days': {'type': 'integer'}},
                'required': ['city']}}

Parameters without a default are required. Map int, float, str, bool to integer, number, string, boolean.

tests.name: describes get_weather
maps every type
tests.code:
def f(a: float, b: bool, c: str, d: int):
    """x"""
p=tool_schema(f)['parameters']['properties']
assert [p[k]['type'] for k in 'abcd']==['number','boolean','string','integer'], f'got {p}'

tests.name: defaults are optional
tests.code:
def f(a: int, b: int = 2, c: str = 'x'):
    """x"""
r=tool_schema(f)['parameters']['required']
assert r==['a'], f'only a has no default, got required={r}'

problems.title: Validate arguments before running
problems.prompt:
Write validate_args(schema, args), returning a list of readable error strings (empty when the arguments are fine). Report a missing required argument, an argument the tool does not have, and a value of the wrong type.

One Python trap: isinstance(True, int) is True, because bool is a subclass of int. A boolean must not pass as an integer or number.

The messages are for the model to read, so make them specific, e.g. "missing argument 'city'".

tests.name: valid arguments pass
missing argument is named
tests.code:
def w(city: str, days: int = 1):
    """x"""
e=validate_args(tool_schema(w), {'days':3})
assert len(e)==1 and 'city' in e[0], f'expected one error naming city, got {e}'

tests.name: unknown argument is reported
tests.code:
def w(city: str):
    """x"""
e=validate_args(tool_schema(w), {'city':'Pune','country':'IN'})
assert len(e)==1 and 'country' in e[0], f'expected one error naming country, got {e}'

tests.name: wrong type is reported
tests.code:
def w(city: str, days: int = 1):
    """x"""
e=validate_args(tool_schema(w), {'city':'Pune','days':'three'})
assert len(e)==1 and 'days' in e[0], f'expected one error naming days, got {e}'

tests.name: a bool is not an integer
tests.code:
def w(days: int):
    """x"""
e=validate_args(tool_schema(w), {'days':True})
assert len(e)==1, f'True must not pass as an integer (bool subclasses int), got {e}'

tests.name: an int is a valid number

problems.title: A dependable agent loop
problems.prompt:
Write run_agent(model, tools, task, max_steps=6, max_obs=200). model(messages) returns either {"answer": ...} or {"tool": name, "args": {...}}. tool_schema and validate_args are provided.

Each step:

  • An answer ends the run with status "answered".
  • The same tool with the same arguments as the previous step ends it with status "stuck".
  • Otherwise produce an observation: an error for an unknown tool or invalid arguments, the tool's result, or the exception the tool raised, all as text starting with "error:" when something went wrong. Never let an exception escape.
  • Truncate observations longer than max_obs to their first max_obs characters plus a note, then append {"role": "tool", "content": obs}.

After max_steps steps without an answer, stop with status "max_steps". Return a dict with status, answer, steps and messages.

tests.name: uses a tool, then answers
tests.code:
m=scripted([{'tool':'get_weather','args':{'city':'Pune'}},{'answer':'31 C'}])
r=run_agent(m,TOOLS,'weather?')
assert r['status']=='answered' and r['answer']=='31 C' and r['steps']==2, f'got {r["status"]}, {r["answer"]}, steps={r["steps"]}'
assert 'Pune' in m.seen[1][-1], f'the second call should see the tool result, saw {m.seen[1]}'

tests.name: invalid arguments become an observation
tests.code:
m=scripted([{'tool':'get_weather','args':{'days':2}},{'answer':'done'}])
r=run_agent(m,TOOLS,'t')
obs=m.seen[1][-1]
assert r['status']=='answered' and obs.startswith('error:') and 'city' in obs, f'expected an error observation naming city, got {obs!r}'

tests.name: tool exceptions do not crash the loop
tests.code:
m=scripted([{'tool':'get_weather','args':{'city':'Pune','days':30}},{'answer':'ok'}])
r=run_agent(m,TOOLS,'t')
obs=m.seen[1][-1]
assert r['status']=='answered' and obs.startswith('error:') and '7' in obs, f'the ValueError should come back as an error observation, got {obs!r}'

tests.name: unknown tools are reported
tests.code:
m=scripted([{'tool':'send_email','args':{}},{'answer':'ok'}])
run_agent(m,TOOLS,'t')
obs=m.seen[1][-1]
assert obs.startswith('error:') and 'send_email' in obs, f'expected an unknown-tool error, got {obs!r}'

tests.name: long observations are truncated
tests.code:
m=scripted([{'tool':'read_log','args':{'path':'app.log'}},{'answer':'ok'}])
run_agent(m,TOOLS,'t',max_obs=200)
obs=m.seen[1][-1]
assert 200<=len(obs)<300 and obs.startswith('INFO ok'), f'expected about 200 chars plus a note, got {len(obs)} chars'

tests.name: repetition is detected
the step budget is enforced
tests.code:
acts=[{'tool':'get_weather','args':{'city':c}} for c in 'ABCDEFGH']
r=run_agent(scripted(acts),TOOLS,'t',max_steps=4)
assert r['status']=='max_steps' and r['steps']==4, f'expected max_steps after 4 steps, got {r["status"]}, {r["steps"]}'

hints: call = (action['tool'], sorted(action.get('args', {}).items())); compare with last_call, then set last_call = call
try: obs = str(tools[name](**args)) except Exception as e: obs = f'error: {type(e).__name__}: {e}'
if len(obs) > max_obs: obs = obs[:max_obs] + f' ...[{len(obs) - max_obs} chars truncated]'
